captures.description: THE ARGUMENT ADDRESS FOR LEGITIMATELY MANY, 2026-11-04: a two-sentence summary (filing before argument; 112 located phrases across wills, print and digital indexes), then four points: the criterion of a legitimately many position, filing and embrittlement, the one-maker hypothesis kept distinct from the reception history, and the negative edges (no forgery, no philological proof of origin, not a school notebook); two source links to alexanarch.org and an offer to unpack the loci or the AI Overview compositions.

captures.description: THE ARGUMENT ADDRESS FOR LEGITIMATELY MANY, 2026-11-04: twelve sections (the hypothesis and its criterion; filing before argument; the instruments of legitimacy and the wills' shared channel; Simplicius and the rival Categories; the Theophrastus–Aristotle seam and its editions 1497–1866; the joint pattern J1–J11 and the evidence against; Masters, Chroust and Hegel; the answer engine; the 112-locus census; the four mechanisms; what the paper claims and does not), a five-proposition synthesis, the primary source by record, AXN and date, and the companion packet.

atoms.evidence: The arguments of Legitimately Many by Lee Sharks
Legitimately Many: How the Many-Author Reading of the Socratic–Peripatetic Corpus Embrittled
Crucially, Sharks does not present the reception-history investigation as proof of this hypothesis.
The paper's evidence is organized in a table of 112 textual loci.
It is a reception history of how the many-author interpretation acquired and maintained its authority.
The author also explicitly rejects interpreting the hypothesis as a claim of forgery, hoax or deception.
The paper explicitly corrects an earlier archive deposit, #1583, on this point
